query: I'm not technical. What does this do? SELECT department, COUNT(*) FROM employees WHERE hire_date >= '2025-01-01' GROUP BY department HAVING COUNT(*) > 5;
expected_behavior: Opens with a one-sentence plain-language summary (departments that hired more than 5 people since January 1, 2025)
Walks through the clauses in everyday words, using piles or a spreadsheet analogy for GROUP BY and HAVING
Notes that the query only reads data and is safe to run

query: Convert this Oracle query to PostgreSQL: SELECT NVL(nickname, first_name) || ' ' || last_name AS display_name FROM people WHERE ROWNUM <= 20;
expected_behavior: Uses COALESCE and LIMIT 20 (or FETCH FIRST 20 ROWS ONLY) in the PostgreSQL version
Warns that Oracle treats empty strings as NULL and that || returns NULL in PostgreSQL when a part is NULL
Notes that ROWNUM without ORDER BY returns an arbitrary 20 rows and suggests adding ORDER BY

expected_behavior: Runs the same filter as a SELECT first to show the affected row count
